reviews.text: It’s stressful and intense in tone, but Sandler’s performance and the confident, stylish direction from the Safdie Brothers keep the film a compelling, if not necessarily easy, viewing experience.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: Put on a pair of headphones and watch it alone in the dark. It’ll be the best, worst experience you’ll have all year.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: Regardless of how and why, Uncut Gems is a unique rollercoaster experience matched by nothing else in 2019.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: While we shake our heads over Ratner’s judgment, it’s hard not to relate to his ambition to bet everything on some malformed vision of the American dream.
reviews.author: PJ Grisar

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is unlike any movie I’ve ever seen before, and more people definitely need to see it. It’s an ugly look at the horror of gambling addiction.
reviews.author: Amy Thomasson

reviews.text: Sandler's portrayal as Howard, the degenerate gambler and jewelry man, makes us garble anxiety with his high energy running around to pay off debts while playing footsie with Kevin Garnett over a stunningly large opal.
reviews.author: Brian Susbielles

reviews.text: Overstuffed on every level—Uncut Gems is definitely not boring, but it’s a lot, more than I can comfortably handle.
reviews.author: Vadim Rizov

reviews.text: Brash, bold and nerve-shredding... It is one of the most intense movie-watching experiences of the year.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: The Safdie brothers’ third act is ferocious, fervent, and one of the most jaw-dropping of the decade.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: If you’re into what the Safdies are doing you’ll probably love this. But for others it will be similar to colonoscopy we see at the very beginning – extremely unpleasant.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Uncut Gems may feel like pure chaos shot into the viewer's brain, but it only seems that way from the countless number of reversals, switches, setbacks, and impulsive choices that befall its protagonist.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is an unforgettable film that plays out like a pulse-pounding Greek tragedy set in 2010s New York.
reviews.author: Toussaint Egan

reviews.text: I gotta admit, now I am in full Safdie Bros. team. It took me this long to see Uncut Gems but I am convinced that the Safdies will save American cinema.
reviews.author: Dustin Chang

reviews.text: Hollywood's dorkiest megastar has never been better.
reviews.author: Alex Flood

reviews.text: It's only been 2 years since The Meyerowitz Stories, so maybe the intervals where Sandler is a little more willing to take risks are growing shorter.
reviews.author: Luiz Oliveira

reviews.text: Adam Sandler is sensational in this intense, nail-biting, adrenaline-fuelled thriller.
reviews.author: Katherine McLaughlin

reviews.text: The Safdie brothers are out to make viewers into balls of stress when watching Uncut Gems; I'll pass on another experience like this one.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Sandler brings his natural likability to the role but layers it with Howard's neurosis, frustration, conniving and even joy. It's a remarkable performance powered by jet fuel
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: None of it's there because it ought to be, it's there because they want it to be.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: The characters are morally bankrupt, which makes it difficult to care about any of their various plights or overall wellbeing - or even their ultimate outcomes.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: "Feels like a constant adrenaline shot to the system"
reviews.author: Shaun Alexander

reviews.text: Not for all tastes, this is a daring piece of cinema that signals a new and welcome direction for Sandler.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: The Safdie brothers had funnyman Adam Sandler showcase his remarkable dramatic chops in this frantic, hyper stressful tale of a New York City jeweller trying to outrun the debt collectors after him.
reviews.author: Film Companion Staff

reviews.text: The casting of Sandler is a stroke of genius.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: Adam Sandler has played straight drama before, but nothing will prepare you for this adrenaline-pumped film that feels like a plunge into a vat of battery acid.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: An anxiety inducing tornado that sweeps you and squirms your brain. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Operates entirely at a level of clammy panic and desperation, forcing its audience to witness a person make all the wrong decisions and being powerless to stop it.
reviews.author: Adam Lubitow

reviews.text: The Safdie brothers' film manages to make me think with that speech, but I cannot empathize with the time-trial misfortunes of the impertinent protagonist. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is a near masterpiece of filmmaking, both in story and style.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: Manic and pulse-pounding, with a blistering energy, this is one hell of a ride.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is driven by a solid performance by Adam Sandler in an enthralling story of gambling addiction. Above anything else, you're watching this to see Adam Sandler shine, and the chaotic drama will only keep you tuned in until the very end.
reviews.author: Emmanuel Noisette

reviews.text: Dizzying in its overlapping talk-talk-talk, incessant ambient din and translucent set design (glass is everywhere), the movie seems to radiate energy, heat, light and pressure -- it crushes scenes into diamonds.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: It's intense filmmaking that starts slow and messy and accelerates to a mesmerising climax.
reviews.author: Simon Weaving

reviews.text: What is there to say? Adam Sandler gives the performance of his career in a sea of diamond-encrusted Furbies.
reviews.author: Laura Bradley

reviews.text: We are rocketed through Ratner's world - a place of permanently raised voices, propulsive camera work and blaring noise - accompanied by a pulsing score from Daniel Lopatin...
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: The Safdie brothers - whose last film, Good Time, redefined Robert Pattinson for a lot of moviegoers - are prepared to show you a new side of Adam Sandler.
reviews.author: Colin Biggs

reviews.text: Adam Sandler, who also did an impressive non-comedy turn in Punch-Drunk Love (2002), puts in a very strong performance as a hard-bitten businessman determined to survive in a world set out to destroy him.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Filmmakers Josh and Benny Safdie bought a quality product to audiences this past year and Sandler shines and the wholly unlikeable Ratner, but the film has flaws.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: The thing that elevates it above all else is the frenetic energy that infuses every scene, yet calibrated so perfectly so that it stays, barely, on the right side of frustrating. There's nothing more thrilling than that.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Uncut Gems isn't exactly an enjoyable experience - it's stressful and hectic and anxiety-provoking. But, that doesn't take away from the fact that the Safdies have created a drama that is downright fascinating.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: Sandler is Oscar-worthy in raw 'Uncut Gems.'
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: The Safdies have not conferred mystical powers onto their film, but like the black opal at its heart, UNCUT GEMS will transfix the viewer by reflecting something a little different back at you depending on what angle you consider it from.
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: The Safdies create dazzling, anxiety-inducing mania that spares no moment for viewers to catch their breath... 10/10 recommend.
reviews.author: Morgan Rojas

reviews.text: It's a brilliantly exhausting movie that gaffer-tapes us to motormouth New York gem dealer and degenerate gambler Howard Ratner... The thrill and despair of the addict are palpable.
reviews.author: Brad Newsome

reviews.text: Possibly one of the most annoying movies I've seen in recent years. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jaime Fa de Lucas

reviews.text: Uncut Gems maintains its social critique and shows us the dirty games played in a society led by capitalism and greed. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: William Venegas

reviews.text: Impressive but somewhat exhausting at 135 minutes, this still has a great deal to admire, from the pitch of nervous tension, to the entire supporting cast.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: Most of us, if we're honest, will see at least a little bit of ourselves - albeit in our worst moments - in Sandler's Ratner, and that is what makes Uncut Gems memorable.
reviews.author: Hannah Brown

reviews.text: I was pleasantly surprised at the choice of material for Adam Sandler and how well he does in the role of Howard.
reviews.author: Marie Asner

reviews.text: The Safdie Brothers manage a constant cranking, winding up of tension, as this escalating situation gets from bad to worse, as Sandler's character makes bad decision after bad decision.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: This is an energy shot of a movie, a dose of which will leave viewers jittery, but craving more.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Fans of The Waterboy should go into Uncut Gems with plenty of high quality H2O to make up for all the juices they'll be projectile-sweating out of their pores.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: If there's something that the Safdies know is how to maintain tension. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Sandler puts everything into his performance. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Martín

reviews.text: A tour de force of nocturnal contingency, and a pulverising cinematic parable on the sheer nauseous toxicity of a life lived on the edge in NYC.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: Adam Sandler, possibly, delivers the most memorable performance of his career. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Philipp Engel

reviews.text: Uncut Gems burns itself right to the wire, leading to an astonishingly tense and funny climax...
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: A free and unleashed Adam Sandler gives us the best performance of his career. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: Adam Sandler shows his versatility delivering a brilliant performance. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge (JJ) Negrete

reviews.text: The glorious outcome, dry and sharp, filmed without underlining, leaves you stunned. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Ocaña

reviews.text: Uncut Gems tethers you, for two hours, to a train wreck of a man as he digs himself into a hole, and then tries to claw his way out of it - painfully, repetitively, unsuccessfully. You're the explosive vest strapped onto the body of a suicide bomber.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Uncut Gems burrows into your pores. It makes you feel unclean, but it's also a rapturous experience; a "rollercoaster of emotions" insofar as the rollercoaster has malfunctioned mid-loop, oscillating back and forth while you're suspended in free-fall.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Despite Adam Sandler doesn't deliver an extraordinary performance, he surprises with this character. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: Equal parts infuriating and exhilarating, Uncut Gems is an accomplished piece of high-anxiety cinema from a pair of filmmakers with a clear knack for the form, a sense of their own, deeply felt excitement emanating from the frame.
reviews.author: Keva York

reviews.text: Equally impacting is the street-smart writing and direction of filmmaking brothers Benny and Josh Safdie, and the mesmerising cinematography of Darius Khondji.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: This is filmmaking of the highest order.
reviews.author: Adrian Hennigan

reviews.text: An anxiety-inducing rollercoaster viewing experience that will truly have your heart racing, 'Uncut Gems' is one of the most unnerving and strangely exhilarating films of recent times.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Adam Sandler carries out a colossal performance as Howard, perfectly embodying that fusion between unbearable but endearing. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel de Partearroyo

reviews.text: Sandler delivers a formidable performance of an annoying winner. [Full review in spanish]
reviews.author: Alonso Díaz de la Vega

reviews.text: Uncut Gems raises the ante in the right ways, without getting close to folding.
reviews.author: Joi Childs

reviews.text: A hugely enjoyable if agitatingly tense tragicomedy.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: An exercise of tension and stress that puts both Sandler's Howard and the audience's nerves to the test. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: A dark parable of a man driven by his demons to make self-destructive choices, likely to elicit radically divided audience reactions, though all will emerge from it feeling as if they've been put through a potent...emotional wringer.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: It's wobbly and looks like it could crack at any moment, and that's part of its charm. It also shines, and when it does, it shines blindingly bright.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: Uncut Gems really nails the anxiety involved in watching sports, and the joy. But while this investment can come from being a noble fan rooting for their home team, there are so many other ways to have skin in the game.
reviews.author: Ade Adeniji

reviews.text: In some quarters this has been declared some sort of minor masterpiece. Me, I'd say it's hard to imagine a more uncomfortable way of spending over two hours in the cinema and advise you to avoid it, shock ending and all.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: A fabulous, uncompromising piece of cinema.
reviews.author: Chris Wasser

reviews.text: It's a loud, sweary, stressful watch and it is really very good.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: It may not be for the faint of heart, but Uncut Gems is a hell of a way to kick-start the new year, like stepping onto a moving streetcar.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Let's just say that Uncut Gems is a heck of a ride.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Having looked at it closely, I'd say it's being over-valued. But not by much.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: It's an endlessly nerve-wracking, visceral assault of a movie that will leave you exhilarated and probably more than a little relieved to be exiting the cinema.
reviews.author: Sarah McIntyre

reviews.text: The Safdies have talent, and if they'd cut this uncut gem they'd get closer to the work they're emulating.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: This is edge-of-the-seat filmmaking, with vertiginous camerawork by Darius Khondji and a relentless, immersive soundscape of electronica and layered dialogue.
reviews.author: Saskia Baron

reviews.text: A terrific, really convincing supporting cast, with not one single character that I didn't believe...
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: The end result is frantic but carefully constructed filmmaking, full of little details that have big pay-offs later on. And Sandler really is astonishing.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: It is extraordinary and unlike any film I've seen in years.
reviews.author: Jamie East

reviews.text: Past the glisten of diamonds and the cocaine mist of Uncut Gems, the Safdie Brothers have a crafted a potent mediation about the cost of our desires.
reviews.author: Michael Lee

reviews.text: This is a white-knuckle ride of a film that never lets up in pace and plot.
reviews.author: Alison Rowat

reviews.text: A time-bomb of foolish compulsion and childlike rage, Sandler maintains our attention and empathy even as his behaviour becomes increasingly moronic and morally impaired.
reviews.author: Kevin Harley

reviews.text: The Safdie brothers have a talent for creating desperate situations for their characters and in turn getting rare and brilliant and unexpected performances for actors you don't see in these roles...
reviews.author: Katie Hogan

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is relentless! It is a non-stop, edge-of-your seat experience.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: When relief finally comes, it's heartbreaking.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: That acerbic, abusive and abrasive script, in which almost everyone is aggressive and annoying, can drive a viewer to distraction.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: Uncut Gems diminishes one of the richest comic sensibilities in modern cinema. It turns Sandler, the smartass who always chooses family and friendship over streetwise selfishness, into an icon of grungy nihilism.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is a brilliant achievement for the two Safdie brothers - it's exciting, entertaining filmmaking, a bittersweet soufflé with a hard centre, well worth seeing for [Adam] Sandler's virtuoso performance alone.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is a fairytale written by the hand of capitalism, where mystical highs are followed by crushing blows -- and there's always a price to pay.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is not only one of the tightest, tensest American thrillers of recent years, but also a fine addition to the New York-set movie canon.
reviews.author: Daniel Green

reviews.text: The things that make Sandler so damn likable are on display, and you empathize with a man who is the textbook definition of unlikable. Sandler's revving on all engines.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Uncut Gems spools out like an Old Testament parable updated for our late-capitalist collapse, a timely tale of greed, envy and idolatry which - like that chunk of mined rock - hides an eternally glimmering truth inside its jagged exterior.
reviews.author: Rick Levin

reviews.text: Invites such total immersion in one corner of New York that the picture takes on an anthropological flavour.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: With an engaging and occasionally surprising visual style and a career-best performance from Adam Sandler, Uncut Gems is truly precious...a gut-punch of a movie.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: This is the year's most exciting film. You can take that to the bank.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: This fantastically unhinged thriller is one of the most exhilarating experiences one is likely to have at the cinema this year.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is good but far from great, an exhausting repetition of watching a sleazy scumbag spiraling out of control by digging himself deeper into a hole.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: There is more to the Safdies' secret sauce than panic. At first glance the cast has the feel of a group of strangers grabbed at random from the sidewalk, yet it clicks and keeps clicking.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: It's relentlessly stressful but as engrossing as hell.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Motor-mouthed along by Sandler's edgy star turn, it's unrewardingly tense.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: Uncut Gems certainly won't be for everyone and you get the sense that's just how the Safdie brothers like it.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: A cunning yet hapless clown juggling 15 balls simultaneously. It'll seriously raise your blood pressure. The question is, do you feel the need to do that? What actually ruined this film for me was the bizarre, '80s-inflected, mostly synthesizer score.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is, somewhat, a raw movie, but quite effective and overwhelming in its approach. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Ponce

reviews.text: 'Uncut Gems' houses what could be Adam Sandler's greatest on-screen performance. Glittering with promise, 'Uncut Gems' is a diamond-sharp crime thriller.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: At a certain point, monotony sets in.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: The twists and turns of "Uncut Gems" are best left untold, but it's a devastating experience. It shows an actor tapping into unexpected depths and establishes the Safdies as true auteurs.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: The Safdie brothers' latest crackles with an uncommonly nervy energy, anchored at all times by Adam Sandler's terrific, career-topping performance.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: The Safdie Brother's impressive vision and storytelling coupled with Adam Sandler's acting prowess and range results in one of the best films of 2019."
reviews.author: Michael Winkler

reviews.text: A monumental thriller, which vividly captures its world's specifics and calibrates its snaky plot for maximum nail-bitability. Also easily the best film to ever extensively feature Adam Sandler yelling at a TV.
reviews.author: Nick De Semlyen

reviews.text: The Safdies, who have sought Sandler for the role of Howard for the better part of a decade, perfectly pen a character to fit the longtime comedic actor's unique quirks...
reviews.author: Matt Ward

reviews.text: Very few recent films can boast this intensity, humor, and unpredictability. And the Safdies attained glory.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is near-perfectly directed & written. Adam Sandler brings his best performance in the crime/sports film, with tension, anxiety and hopelessness dialing up with each minute.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: I'm not on the "Give Adam Sandler an Oscar nomination" bandwagon -- I've easily seen at least five leading male performances more varied and more interesting -- but he's certainly up to the task presented to him by the Safdies.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: ...a dazzling array of disorientation.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is full of surprises more fulfilling than the movie's main narrative, from its production design and cinematography to supporting turns from Idina Menzel and Eric Bogosian.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: Watching Adam Sandler is like watching a sped up version of dodge ball, talking non-stop to justify his every move. And once you get into his rhythm, it's hard to look away.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Perhaps the most enjoyable film to be this relentlessly unpleasant to watch, Uncut Gems has the sound and feel of a hurried fork stabbing at and missing food while on a blind date your mom set up.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: My only criticism is that the film takes a long time to play out. Even so, it's a movie that commands your attention & lingers afterwards, as does Sandler's intensely focused performance. This tops everything he's done before & is worthy of an Oscar.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: Sandler is fascinating to watch in this role as the shady wheeler dealer Howard Ratner. He whipsaws from manic emotional highs, tenderness and mischief to devastating lows. Watching Ratner desperately juggle bets and deals is something to behold.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Uncut Gems' episodic structure paves the way for an exceedingly erratic midsection that's rarely as engrossing and tense as one might've anticipated...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is tense, sleaze-filled trip through the dark underbelly of New York's Jeweler's Row. Sandler is gloriously unhinged on screen in what is hands-down the performance of his lifetime.
reviews.author: Dan Tabor

reviews.text: The Safdie Brothers prove once again they are directors to watch. Adam Sandler is exceptional and Julia Fox gives the breakout performance of the year.
reviews.author: Lauren Veneziani

reviews.text: Lord knows I disliked this movie. My ears were ringing by the time I escaped. But I do have to hand it to Adam Sandler. He delivered an unexpected performance.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: A well-written film, and one of the best crime films I've seen in a while. They take a lot of the tropes you expect and flip them on your head.
reviews.author: Kristian Harloff

reviews.text: The movie has a great, frantic pace to it...but it could have been shorter, maybe because they spent so much time with The Weeknd...I also wish it had another conclusion...
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: This is really something ambitious, different. And it's good to see.
reviews.author: Martin Thomas

reviews.text: [Adam] Sandler brilliantly creates Ratner, pushing his own boundaries and exhausting us as we watch. He's crude. His language is as offensive as his actions, but there is a reality to him that is not only intriguing but engaging.
reviews.author: Pamela Powell

reviews.text: It's a full-bodied role born by the Brothers Safdie (Josh and Benny), capitalizing on both Sandler's manic obnoxiousness and tender underbelly.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Uncut Gems should be lauded for its commitment to embracing nihilism and chaos.
reviews.author: Michelle Kisner

reviews.text: Real art has a distinctive point of view and the courage to stand by it. Uncut Gems is art and it's one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: Shrill, monotonous, the usual half-baked, phony Scorsese wannabe nonsense from the overrated Safdie brothers.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Through it all, [Adam] Sandler's Ratner bobs and weaves and fast talks his way in and out of corners, until the rooms in which he lives, works, and plays are all metaphorically round.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Sandler's [...] charisma and humor give you someone to root for in spite of yourself, and his obnoxiousness keeps you from feeling too bad when he inevitably gets clocked.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: It's far too rare to find films like this that explore real worlds and people that are, to this point, unexplored territory. A frantic, masterful, delight.
reviews.author: Richard Bardon

reviews.text: There are very few young filmmakers these days who truly 'get it' as much as the Safdies. Their commitment to authenticity sets them apart in a big way, and Uncut Gems is their crowning achievement thus far.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: Every character, no matter how minor, seethes with inner life; the dialogue is vibrant, startling and unique, the milieu beyond evocative and fuelled by integrity, the camerawork energetic and artful, the score wondrous, and the pacing magnificent.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Adam Sandler doing the absolute best work of his career. Really, truly when given the challenge, he more than rises to it.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: The Safdie Brothers have crafted a corrosive love song to the hustlers, grifters and rancid mad risk takers who made America great.
reviews.author: Dorothy Woodend

reviews.text: Somehow this too feels all too real, thanks to the Safdie's confident work and Sandler's astounding performance.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: There is a lot to admire in "Uncut Gems".
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: Sandler, who has proved his worth as a dramatic actor before, has never been better, or funnier, than he is here.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: ... an endurance test foreshadowing the final five minutes of the film; while observant viewers won't be too surprised by the plot, they might be by the performance.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: One of the great talents of the Safdies is to show you New York from the inside. With their films you always feel like you're getting the worm's-eye view, an underground tour of where stuff actually happens.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: To say that Sandler has never been better doesn't quite explain what he's accomplished in Uncut Gems.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: This is the Sandler I wish we would see more of, an actor willing to go outside his comfort zone and take chances.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: [Sandler gives] a terrific performance in a movie often too noisy for its own good.
reviews.author: Matthew Singer

reviews.text: It's one of the year's most annoying movies.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: It's a film I can't help thinking about so now I'm itching to see it again and willing to put myself through this exquisitely well-crafted ringer one more time.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: Sandler is terrific in this role, a flop-sweat-soaked comedy of brutality punctuated by punches to the face.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: It's remarkable in many ways, and yet undoubtedly it got on my nerves.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: [The film] takes a critical, yet sympathetic look at a seriously flawed, but not completely un-redeemable human being. An uncut gem indeed.
reviews.author: Kathy Fennessy

reviews.text: [Sandler is] really, really effective as a Diamond District hustler...That said, the latest from the writing/directing Safdie Brothers (Benny and Josh) is like having an irate New Yawk cabbie screaming nonstop in your ear for two-plus hours.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: He's (Sandler) the center stone in an exciting chaos of a story that grabs your attention and refuses to let go.
reviews.author: Maria Sciullo

reviews.text: The performances are good, everything felt authentic.
reviews.author: Tony Baker

reviews.text: Feels like Harold stepped off the pages of a Dostoyevsky novel and landed in the streets of New York City. And Sandler makes a meal out of it.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is a hidden gem.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: What holds it all together, besides a fine ensemble peppered with a bevy of nonprofessionals, is the moody cinematography by Darius Khondji and Daniel Lopatin's edgy, retro score.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: The Sadies virtually dare us to keep pace.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Adam Sandler gives a career-best performance and turns 'Uncut Gems' into a two-hour panic attack.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: It's a breathless journey that captures the exhilaration and the hopelessness of living life on the edge. It's a gamble that pays off, and then some.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: The Safdie brothers deliver another high-intensity rollercoaster ride with Adam Sandler's best performance of his career.
reviews.author: Sharronda Williams

reviews.text: Brimming with unbridled energy, the Safdie brothers wield the pulse of New York City and use it to drive their unorthodox method of storytelling. Sandler is out of his element and phenomenal.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Famous for playing annoying louts in comedies, Adam Sandler goes viscerally dramatic as a grating gambling addict in 'Uncut Gems.'
reviews.author: John Wirt

reviews.text: It's frantic, loud, and several kinds of -pulsive, including (but not limited to) pro-, com- and re-.
reviews.author: Jay Stone

reviews.text: Sandler is quite good in the role, all but disappearing into the character. (Full Content Review for Parents - Violence, Profanity, Sexual Content, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Cinematographer Darius Khondji gives the film a gritty, twitchy feel. The Safdies give it a story and a pace that never lets up. But Sandler gives it life, and makes "Uncut Gems" a must-see movie.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: It grabs you by the scruff of the neck, trips you and stomps you in the gut.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: This rough gem may be uncut, but it's sharp and will make you bleed.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Adam Sandler gives the best performance of his career in this exhilarating and ruthless, hell of a ride. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Uncut Gems confronts its audience with the idea that, perhaps deep down, we like to see bad people getting away with it [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: There is nothing polite about brothers Benny Safdie and Josh Safdie's newest hyper-adrenalized ticking clock drama Uncut Gems.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: A stark, turbulent and mesmerizing ride-along with one man's futile navigation of late capitalism's darker and more fickle realms.
reviews.author: Josh Goller

reviews.text: Adam Sandler does award-worthy work as a jeweler addicted to the gambling rush.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Exhausting and exhilarating, the sort of film that takes the idea of escapism and pushes it to a nearly nauseating degree. We enjoy Howard's exploits because it is thrilling to watch someone get away with it, even if we aren't exactly rooting for him.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Love or hate Sandler's degnerate gambler/jeweler, his compulsions are so widespread your own eyes get compelled to stay glued to the screen.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: A total knockout - both in that it's a wallop of a film and may inspire a well-deserved nap due to exhaustion shortly after the end credits roll.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: A masterpiece.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: When Adam Sandler decides to bag the fart jokes and really act, few actors are better. This is an intense, almost exhausting drama and one of my favorite movies this year.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: There is real cinematic tension in this own-worst-enemy tale of addiction and its ever escalating series of bad bets. But Adam Sandler's unfettered arrogance renders it far from endearing or fun.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: A pretty entertaining film with an absolutely amazing last act.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: The Gambler for a new generation, that classic film doesn't conjure up a fraction of the desperation andanxiety created byUncut Gems..
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: This is the best character Sandler has ever played.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Sandler inhabits this character fully and without vanity, working Howard's ready smile and desperate eyes and needling, never-ending sales pitch into a devastating portrait of a lesser shark, the kind who's always late for the kill.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: The Safdie Brothers' UNCUT GEMS is the best panic attack you'll enjoy all year. Brilliant character study, engaging story that is constantly twisting, and also one of the top films of 2019.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: "Uncut Gems" is a monster of a movie.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: In "Uncut Gems," Benny and Josh Safdie allow (Sandler) to unleash the manic persona he brings to his comedy in a dramatic forum. And Sandler rises to the occasion. You simultaneously despise him yet admire him for his chutzpah.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Exhilarating filmmaking, like a two-hour anxiety attack. It's unlikely you'll see anything this tightly-wound at the theatre anytime soon.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: Excruciating, repulsive, and utterly exhilarating.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: The plot behind Uncut Gems' race against the clock is firmly entrenched in a meticulously planned out escalation of connected events.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: It all ends up to be a film in which both Sandler and the Safdies are pulling out all the stops, and it works.
reviews.author: Ed Symkus

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is a high-wire act of mood and energy, and it will pummel your senses. It's also one of the best movies of 2019, if you can endure it.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Like a rickety roller coaster, it's a heady ride while it lasts, but you're kinda glad when it's over.
reviews.author: Neil Morris

reviews.text: [Sandler] has perhaps his second-best-ever role (after Punch-Drunk Love) in Benny and Josh Safdie's frantic, caffeinated 'Uncut Gems.'
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: The headline ... is Sandler. It's not just that the role is great for him; he's great for it, adding humor, desperation and charm in deft fashion.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Will more than likely leave you in a cold sweat.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: It's the cinematic equivalent to mixing cocaine with acid, a burst of energy that unfolds like a dream.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: The Safdie Brothers have figured out how to make chaos a genre...An award-worthy performance from Adam Sandler.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: I wanted out, even as I couldn't look away.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Sandler is so good as Howard, this perpetual schemer and hustler, that it's unsettling.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: As with their previous film Good Time, the brother-directors Josh and Bennie Safdie have a wonderful gift for capturing desperate lives spinning even further out of control.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: Sandler is so good, so committed and so watchable that, despite everything - Howard's irrationality, a rogue's gallery of unpleasant characters, the foreboding of a bad, bad end - you can't take your eyes off the screen, which Sandler seldom vacates.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: The Safdies aren't interested in morality tales but amorality tales, and their stories' no-holds-barred recklessness, while at first freeing, steadily grows exhausting. Thankfully, the Safdies also know how to shoot, cut, and score like nobody else.
reviews.author: Erik Henriksen

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is a triumph of building a world and a character that are so infused with each other that they are impossible to separate.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: Uncut Gems works as a perfectly pitched period piece about a bygone gilded age, halfway through the Obama years, the sheen of Hope and Change slightly dulled...
reviews.author: Nadine Smith

reviews.text: The Safdies deliver another shot of adrenaline straight to the heart with Uncut Gems.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: An original and pulsating odyssey about fate and those who accept to challenge it. Its complex and riveting character study allows Sandler to showcase his acting chops. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Directors Benny and Josh Safdie double down on the pure rush of their 2017 success Good Time with this adrenaline-soaked thriller.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: The vivid vulgarity is so repetitive that it ceases to be shocking, the chaotic plot is predictable and Adam Sandler's character is a totally self-indulgent, utterly contemptible scumbag. Spending two hours in his company is sheer agony.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: By the time it's all over, nothing is exactly what you might feel. But Sandler and Fox give it the humanity the Safdies wanted there.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: It may just be the movie you've been waiting for.
reviews.author: Scott Wampler

reviews.text: It's the kind of movie that burrows deep into your brain and demands that you watch it again. Sure, you feel dirty after placing your bet, but it's a small price to pay for such a wild ride.
reviews.author: J.R. Kinnard

reviews.text: Adam Sandler almost always plays Adam Sandler, a likable, sometimes funny jokester. But when he steps away from that, as he does in Uncut Gems, he proves that he is a true actor.
reviews.author: Chuck Yarborough

reviews.text: Bolstered by great performances from [Adam] Sandler, [Kevin] Garrett, and LaKeith Stanfield, Uncut Gems will have you on the edge of the seat the entire time.
reviews.author: Katey Stoetzel

reviews.text: Intriguingly, it's a personal story without any reverberating themes, and yet it still leaves us shaken.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is easily among the year's best movies. Instantly engaging, it's a masterfully crafted run across the edge of a blade that never lets up.
reviews.author: Justin Jones

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is a breathless film; it will literally take your breath away. It's almost panic attack -inducing and at the very least, heart-rate increasingly tense, a viscerally physical cinema experience.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: The Safdies have a preferred aesthetic and mood and remain true to it throughout. For those who appreciate this sort of modern-day neo noir experience, it gleams as hypnotically as the titular totem.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: The Safdies certainly know how to litter the frame with kinetic energy, but while everything is moving, there just isn't any depth to things.
reviews.author: Kristen Lopez

reviews.text: Yes, it builds tension, but I don't think it's a huge stretch for Adam Sandler to be obnoxious. A lot of it I just wasn't buying.
reviews.author: Charles Solomon

reviews.text: It is quite good. Intensity is the thing that the Safdie brothers work with. They start a film out going at 60mph and keep applying the gas.
reviews.author: Tim Cogshell

reviews.text: [The] use of Adam Sandler is just outstanding. I've never seen his tightly-coiled intensity worked to better effect than it does here.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: Despite what the title suggests, it's more of an impeccably crafted diamond, with a multifaceted brilliance that only comes from a masterwork.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is terrifically effective as you're watching it, though its aroma-unlike streetside garbage in the summer-might not linger.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is so chock-full of Chekhov's guns, it could arm a small country.
reviews.author: Emily Heller

reviews.text: [An] excellent new film.
reviews.author: Kevin Nguyen

reviews.text: A vivid simulation of what it might be like to live inside a pinball machine, giving Adam Sandler his showiest role, which he embraces obvious appreciation.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: He's [Sandler] never been as impressive as he is as the New York jeweler, gambler, dreamer and self-defeating buffoon Howard Ratner in Uncut Gems.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: Uncut Gems provides Adam Sandler with the performance of a lifetime coupled with anxiety, stress driven spot on filmmaking by Benny and Josh Safdie.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: The magic trick of the Safdies is that even when they plunge you into the dyspeptic, spleeny, cyclical hell of Howard's own making, they manage to make you root for him anyway.
reviews.author: Soraya Nadia McDonald

reviews.text: The Safdie Brothers' nervy ball of tension sends a hustler (Adam Sandler) blasting recklessly through a city where everybody is on the make.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: As for Sandler, he deserves the accolades he's getting, again proving that with the right material, he has an uncanny ability to reach deep within us, despite our deep, DEEP annoyance.
reviews.author: Jocelyn Noveck

reviews.text: It may confound and even anger some viewers, but the Safdie brothers know what they're doing. They want their gripping story to put us between a rock and a hard place and make us squirm, just like their protagonist.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: An effervescent tale of self-destructing behavior, anchored by Sandler's intense performance. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is a dose of high anxiety filmmaking that's partly Shakespearean tragedy of hubris and part underbelly crime saga...
reviews.author: Chris Feil

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is easily the most immersive movie-going experience you'll have this year -- if not ever.
reviews.author: Brett Arnold

reviews.text: Everything is simultaneously terrifying, horrifying and mesmerizing in Mr. Sandler's new movie. Uncut Gems is a dark sparkler.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Howard is nothing but drive and, for 134 adrenalized, unflinching, emotionally and physically thrilling minutes, we get to ride along with him.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: "Uncut Gems" insists on keeping audiences on tenterhooks as Howard tries to play the ends against the middle - or just stay one step ahead of his enemies-waiting for his windfall....viewers may be wise to bring a case of Tums to chew on.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is a massive achievement and [the Safdies'] best movie yet.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: It's the right movie for the right person at the right time, a thing of strange beauty forged under a mountain of heat, pressure, and irritation.
reviews.author: Andrew Lapin

reviews.text: I loved Uncut Gems. It's a brutal watch, and my nerves are still too frazzled to see it again, but I will.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: If anything, Ratner appears as a perfect product of assimilation, a pure animal of commerce, monomaniacally focused on winning and living for the Art of the Deal.
reviews.author: Nick Pinkerton

reviews.text: We don't have to like the guy. We just have to understand Howard, and Uncut Gems ... really makes us understand him.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The fullest expression of Sandler and his singular talents that we have witnessed in his sometimes confounding and often infuriating 30-plus-year career.
reviews.author: Oliver Jones

reviews.text: The story's unrelenting nature works against it, blunting the lure of seeing Adam Sandler in one of his occasional dramatic performances -- a showy role, yes, but in a movie that proves all that glitters is not gold.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: It doesn't seem to add up to much - a little man lives his life - but this is just enough.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: It's gleefully anarchic and determined to leave you exhausted. Mission accomplished.
reviews.author: Taylor Antrim

reviews.text: Directed with relentless tension and diamond-hard intelligence by Josh and Benny Safdie, "Uncut Gems" is a thriller and a character study, a tragedy and a blast.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: The Safdies have a magic touch with unpleasantness. They can find pure human tragedy in the most baroque modern horrors, buried like diamonds within the rock.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Sandler's gut-punch, in-your-face performance smashes through the comedy ceiling of stunted man-child schlub roles that have mostly defined his acting career.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: The Safdies have designed Uncut Gems with knife's edge precision to tear audiences' nerves to shreds, and the results are as gripping as they are exhausting.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: The Safdie Brothers have meticulously created one of the year's most intentionally irritating films.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: Sandler gambling drama is profane, violent, and lewd.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: Watching Uncut Gems is like having an anxiety attack that lasts 135 minutes. An exhilarating, electrifying tale.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: A vivid crime thriller featuring a fever-pitch performance by Sandler.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: An edge of your seat nail-biter - a tour de force from The Safdie Bros and Adam Sandler. Julia Fox is a standout as well.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: A 135-minute exercise in anxiety and unpleasantness. It begins with a colonoscopy, and things go downhill from there.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Offers 100% glorious chaos for 130 minutes as the story follows one trouble man's desire for redemption he hasn't earned.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Josh and Benny Safdie have crafted another crazed, flavorful, cinematic slug of hooch. At the end of the movie, I felt a slight hangover rather than satisfaction -- a dazed sense of, "Wow, what was the point of all that?" Still, I enjoyed the binge.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: The most anxiety filled trip to the cinema I had this year... and I loved it.
reviews.author: Rosalie Kicks

reviews.text: Uncut Gems was my most stressful cinematic experience of 2019. It was also one of the best.
reviews.author: Hannah Lodge

reviews.text: As a Manhattan jeweler and gambling addict caught in a vise of his own making, Adam Sandler proves he can act with the best of them, meeting every challenge the incendiary Safde brothers throw at him to give the audience the ride of its life.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Sandler's never been better, really, balancing speedwalking desperation and fast-talking salesmanship with sorrow and glee.
reviews.author: Darren Franich

reviews.text: Howie, with all of his flaws and his flawed wardrobe, is just like the rest of us...you hate to love it.
reviews.author: Liana Satenstein

reviews.text: The building panic and tension releasing in a cathartic explosion that left me feeling not just relieved but actually kind of pumped? Maybe that speaks more to my own mental health quirks, but regardless, Uncut Gems is worth a watch.
reviews.author: Brittany Knupper

reviews.text: Certainly Uncut Gems is the product of an uncompromising vision. But I found the result to be claustrophobic and, finally, dull...
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: Adam Sandler deserves an Oscar for his riveting performance in "Uncut Gems." He's absolutely brilliant here.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Like a more Jewish-themed Bad Lieutenant with all the intensity and half the sensationalism -- also, Adam Sandler. Uncut Gems is one of the best of the decade.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: [A] recklessly audacious and wildly accomplished blend of crime thriller, family melodrama, and sports drama.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: How'd we end up in a place where the new crime movie starring Happy Gilmore, the voice of Elsa and the power forward for the '07 to 2013 Celtics is... honestly kinda BETTER than the new crime movie starring DeNiro, Pacino and Joe Pesci?
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: It's excruciating and exhilarating.
reviews.author: Sheila O'Malley

reviews.text: It's impressive just how much the Safdies are able to make you squirm without making you run out of the theater. Uncut Gems is a train wreck. Just one you can't take your eyes off of. That's a compliment of the highest degree.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is master class filmmaking from every conceivable aspect; if Martin Scorsese was the cinematic revolution of his time, the Safdie Brothers are modern-day insurgents
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Impacted with a certain NYC chutzpah that keeps it always hopping with never ending angles, slimy characters and dirty incidents.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: may be unlike anything you've experienced, as if the helicopter sequence in Martin Scorsese's "Goodfellas" were extended to feature film length... Be prepared to strap yourself onto a cinematic rocket.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: [Adam] Sandler's eyes twinkle with adrenaline. He isn't funny, but absolutely everything he does is worthy of laughter. It can get overwhelming. His performance is a gift.
reviews.author: Dom Sinacola

reviews.text: The Safdie brothers continue their winning streak of making harshly real films about everyday New Yorkers with fatal flaws. But this time, they've also given Adam Sandler a platform to show just how good he is with the right collaborators.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: Rarely have I been further on the edge of my seat watching a film like this unfold.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is a film that literally won't let you get up from your seat until the final credits. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: The Safdie brothers have served up an ear blasting, soul piercing, and pretty damn thrilling take on how the American Dream can go very, very wrong.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: It gets on your nerves in the best way.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: Probably the most rotten fresh I've given. Uncut Gems is good but it's a tough viewing that I still don't know if I fully enjoyed
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: Powered by Adam Sandler's note-perfect turn, Uncut Gems is a stylishly scuzzy work that's as propulsive as it is maddening and exhausting.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: The unique genius of the Safdie Bros is that they can put Adam Sandler in one of his best dramatic roles to date and still start the movie with a classic Sandman butthole joke.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: If your taste runs to over-the-top movies like "The Wolf of Wall Street," "Inglorious Basterds," and "Dolemite is My Name," this movie is for you. Adam Sandler can match this year's Eddie Murphy with ease.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: You will squirm, you will hurt, and you'll respect the hell out of Adam Sandler's ability to bring the worst out of his surrounding actors in the best possible way.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: He's Icarus in a gold chain and a Celtics jersey. But that's the vertiginous, pulse-pounding thrill of Uncut Gems.
reviews.author: Isaac Feldberg

reviews.text: Maybe there is a mystical power in this nutty movie that takes archetypes, genre staples, and even movie stars and builds from their raw materials something wholly original, and coolly dazzling.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: This felt like a one-of-a-kind experience thanks to the Safdie brothers' style.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: A heart-pounding, nerve-shredding, funny masterpiece with a compelling, all-time best performance from Sandler. Uncut Gems is a truly electrifying trip which should catapult the Safdie brothers into the mainstream as experts of high-octane cinema.
reviews.author: Luke Channell

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is utterly relentless from start to finish; a true force of nature that is excruciating to sit through yet impossible to look away from.
reviews.author: Dan Barnes

reviews.text: We don't know quite how it will play out, but half the victory is in the experience of watching it. And for Uncut Gems, it more than earns the roller coaster it puts its audience on.
reviews.author: Michelle Jaworski

reviews.text: With Uncut Gems, the Safdies are operating on another level entirely, making a film that is, quite simply, a force of nature.
reviews.author: Jack Blackwell

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is an acquired taste as it aims to provoke audience anxiety and concern, but those in its thrall are rewarded with laugh-out-loud moments, the edge of your seat tension, and a great showcase for Adam Sandler's talents.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: The finest film yet from the Safdie Brothers, and one that rewards any audiences who remain after the audacious, abrasive opening. Well, "rewards" might not be the best word for it - you'll definitely need a stiff drink and a sit down afterwards.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is an utterly incoherent mess, it's one of the worst films I've seen in a long time.
reviews.author: Ben Rolph

reviews.text: An almost surreally abrasive thrill right now, it feels like a time capsule for film-loving generations to come - providing they can last until the end of it.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: The film goes deeper than the brothers ever have into a genuine affection for their various schemers, and that makes all the difference.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: In 2019, the Waterboy has become a man.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is a prime slab of concentrated pulp storytelling in 135 New York minutes, gripping and remorseless, and probably the cruellest, funniest joke of Adam Sandler's career.
reviews.author: Tom Charity

reviews.text: Uncut Gems isn't just a sadistic portrait of mistakes and punishment. There's a curiosity to dig deeper behind all that glitters; deep inside the gem, far under the skin.
reviews.author: Ella Kemp

reviews.text: Directors Josh and Benny Safdie guide us down a glittering rabbit hole into the heart of a precious opal to begin this masterful work of filmmaking, and leave us there stunned by its brilliance.
reviews.author: Caitlin Quinlan

reviews.text: The movie is dark and wickedly funny. And Uncut Gems is long but never drags; there's so much propulsive, forward momentum even when the characters never get anywhere.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: Uncut Gems it's an adrenaline-spiked gauntlet from which you can't escape, but when you come out on the other side, you feel glad you took the ride.
reviews.author: Rafael Motamayor

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is everything you'd expect and hope for from the Safdie Brothers. It will get your heart rate going and replace your morning coffee.
reviews.author: Brent Goldman

reviews.text: Sandler delivers a tour de force performance in one of the year's best films.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: Even as they prevent the narrative from hurtling off the tracks, the Safdies keep plunging Howard-and the audience-downward, culminating in a final shot that, magically, comes out the other side.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: Yet another astonishing display of Sandler's range and the Safdies' skills...
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: An exhilarating, anxiety-inducting thrill ride bound to stress you out and inject you with a good time.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: "Uncut Gems" is the equivalent of a cinematic anxiety attack taking its toll on your senses. Pop a couple aspirins, bring a reliable pair of ear plugs, and watch as Adam Sandler has just pushed himself into the crowded Oscar race.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Rarely do movies chronicle any synergy between Blacks and Jews who are both living on the same edge. Brilliant filmmaking. [Adam] Sandler deserves an Oscar nod and an apology from past naysayers.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: It's that rarity of a film that believes it's smarter than you and then proves it.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: A Safdie Brothers movie isn't a Safdie Brothers movie if it doesn't stress you the hell out, and Uncut Gems does just that.
reviews.author: Oliver Whitney

reviews.text: The Safdie Brothers' thriller is a raw and powerful feat of filmmaking anchored by a career-best Adam Sandler performance.
reviews.author: Anna Swanson

reviews.text: Adam Sandler demonstrates that he is more than capable to bring in a magnificent performance with a character that lives on the border between comedy and tragedy. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: María Fernanda Mugica

reviews.text: Craftier direction could maintain the separation between viewer and subject while still conveying the sense of agitation omnisciently, without dragging us through the depths of Howard's self-dealt miseries.
reviews.author: Rubin Safaya

reviews.text: It's an absolute train wreck watch, and it's a career-best for Sandler.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: With the new movie from the Safdie brothers, Adam Sandler reminds us once again that he's not a bad actor. He's only done some really bad movies. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Orlando Maldonado

reviews.text: Adam Sandler gives the kind of performance that revitalizes a career in the bold, propulsive epic.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Between the Robert Altmanesque sound mix with conversations jumbled on top of each other, the camera that remains jittery even in quiet moments and music that uses stately choral passages not to lull but to disrupt, the Safdies are maestros of messiness.
reviews.author: Steve Pond

reviews.text: A 134-minute anxiety attack disguised as a movie, Benny and Josh Safdie's Uncut Gems is a New York trash-terpiece.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: The frantic adjective does not even begin to describe the energy with which the Safdie brothers direct this comic thriller. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Leonardo Garcia Tsao

reviews.text: In the end, it all comes back to Howard, who Sandler makes frustrating and captivating in equal measure.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: Adam Sandler delivers one of his very best physical performances as Howard, making us genuinely feel every heated exasperation and crushing failure of his as he schemes and sweats his way all across New York City.
reviews.author: Josh Lewis

reviews.text: Adam Sandler's stunning performance and an effective finale are enough to forgive the Safdie Bros. for making a movie aimed at purposefully annoying you and making you want to cover your ears
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: It's a performance as live-wire exciting as the one the Safdies got out of Robert Pattinson in Good Time. And the movie itself is exhilarating. Just bring a Xanax.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: The Safdie Brothers love to make movies about down-and-out folks making one terrible choice after another.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: It's a rich, enthralling and utterly demented experience...
reviews.author: Kambole Campbell

reviews.text: ...Adam Sandler delivers the performance of his life in Uncut Gems.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: In the film, a man's individual tragedy illuminates the emptiness of the systems that define him.
reviews.author: Jake Cole

reviews.text: The Safdies' new movie is loud and exhausting, but Sandler is perfectly cast.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: My idea of Sandler and what he represents quickly faded once the film began.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: A jangling panic attack of a movie and a timely reminder that, when he puts his mind to it, Adam Sandler can be one of the finest actors currently working.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: It's a bruising, desperate anxiety attack of a film that rips the rug out from under you when you least expect it. And, because it really cannot be said enough: Adam Sandler is on the form of his life.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: It wouldn't be inappropriate to call this thoroughly on-steroids film an edge-of-your-seat experience.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: Uncut Gems is a pulse-pounding film that is as captivating as it is disorienting.
reviews.author: Scott Menzel

reviews.text: Classic Safdie characters are brash, volatile-as are Sandler's. Here, juiced up with an awful mustache and a personal style befitting his awful merchandise, he unleashes untold reserves of mania and panic.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Suggests "Mean Streets" by way of Preston Sturges, with a touch of "Death of a Salesman" to boot - a mesmerizing chronicle of desperate schemes, and it's hard to imagine anyone but Sandler at the center of it.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: "Uncut Gems" feels like being locked inside the pinwheeling brain of a lunatic for more than two hours - and guess what: It's a gas!
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Uncut Gems emerges as real gem itself, a sparkling comedy-drama about a compulsive gambler and risk-taker who never knows when to quit.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: Dizzying, but engrossing and entertaining, Uncut Gems is a glorious film that showcases Adam Sandler at his finest.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

synopsis: A charismatic jeweler makes a high-stakes bet that could lead to the windfall of a lifetime. In a precarious high-wire act, he must balance business, family and adversaries on all sides in pursuit of the ultimate win.
